title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning for queuing fairness, starvation prevention, and timeouts
author: Asha Nair
description: Motivation: Continuous-batcher was showing unfair queueing behaviour under mixed workloads (many small low-volume streams + a few high-throughput clients). Low-volume streams were frequently starved and observed intermittent tail latency spikes when high-throughput groups monopolized batching windows. This PR introduces scheduler-level tuning to improve queueing fairness, add starvation prevention, and make request timeouts more robust. Summary of changes: 1) Scheduler tunables: add fairness_weight (per-class priority weight), max_queue_time_ms (hard cap on how long a request may wait before being forced into the next batch), and starvation_threshold_ms (age after which a request is prioritized). Defaults chosen to be conservative and backward-compatible with existing behavior. 2) Preemption+aging: implement light-weight preemption where a batch can be slightly rebalanced to include aged requests when the starvation threshold is exceeded. This is a bounded operation to avoid destabilizing throughput. 3) Timeout enforcement: add strict per-request queue timeout propagation so that callers get timely failures rather than long waits; also added a server-side enqueue-time metric and a separate queue_timeout_exceeded counter. 4) KV cache eviction hint: expose an optional eviction_hint on KV cache lookups so the batcher can deprioritize requests likely to miss cache or prefer cached prefixes, improving overall token cost efficiency. 5) Metrics and observability: new metrics (batcher.queue_age_p50/p95/p99, batcher.starved_requests_total, batcher.force_flushed_batches_total). 6) Tests: unit tests for scheduler invariants, integration test that reproduces starvation scenario, and perf harness (microbench) to measure delta across workloads. 7) Docs: add configuration docs with recommended defaults and guidance for tuning by workload. Performance: internal perf runs across mixed workloads show ~20% reduction in P95 request enqueue-to-dispatch latency for low-volume streams and a 5-8% throughput improvement in stable steady-state due to better batching decisions. No notable regression on high-throughput-only workloads. Compatibility: all new config fields are optional and default to previous behaviour; no API contract changes. Rollout: feature guarded behind config flags and enabled on canary nodes first. See release notes and rollout plan in linked Linear tickets.

release_notes: Improved continuous-batcher scheduler: added tunable fairness and starvation prevention knobs (fairness_weight, max_queue_time_ms, starvation_threshold_ms), bounded preemption to avoid low-volume stream starvation, stricter queue timeout enforcement, and new metrics to observe batching fairness. Backwards-compatible defaults. See docs/continuous-batcher.md for tuning guidance.
